articleTitle: British Standard relating to static due to material handling
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrostatic Problems During Material Handling
abstract: The British Standard BS5958 entitled 'Control of Undesirable Static Electricity' was published in 1991. Part I deals with the basic aspects of charge generation and the retention of undesirable static electricity in solids, liquids and gases and also on people. Part II deals with the generation of static electricity in particular situations during the handling of different types of materials which includes liquids, powders, gases, sprays, explosives and electro-explosive devices. Several examples are given to illustrate both the basic principles of charge accumulation in particular industrial situations and incidents. The ways are discussed in which as assessment of minimum ignition energy (MIE) can be made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The electrostatic behaviour of clothing fabrics containing electrically conducting threads
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrostatic Problems During Material Handling
abstract: This paper examines the antistatic behaviour of a selection of fabrics in terms of their suitability for use in flammable atmospheres and in clean rooms. Three sets of fabric are examined each containing different types of antistatic thread in grid patterns with spacings of 5, 10 and 20 mm. Two of the sets of plain woven, continuous filament polyester yarn. The third set is a plain wave of continuous filament nylon yarn.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrostatic Problems During Material Handling
abstract: The two incidents described were chosen because they were both thoroughly investigated, the mechanisms involved were unusual but may be relevant to other industrial situations and, in both instances, the mechanism that caused the ignitions could be reproduced. They relate to explosions of handlamps considered safe in flammable atmospheres and of lead/acid batteries during removal of plastic labels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurements for the assessment of ignition risks from static electricity
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrostatic Problems During Material Handling
abstract: Practical work is described to test two approaches devised for avoiding risks of ignition during mechanical mixing, in flammable atmospheres, of materials which easily become highly charged. The approaches are: first, changes to the sequence of production operations to segregate periods of high static charge generation from the time when flammable atmospheres are present; second, use of additives to modify the charge decay rates of critical materials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrostatic Problems During Material Handling
abstract: The principle hazards associated with the application of powder coatings are listed, and safe working practices are set out for the prevention of ignition by spark or flame.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hazards associated with filling and emptying flexible intermediate bulk containers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrostatic Problems During Material Handling
abstract: The use of flexible intermediate bulk containers (FIBC) for storage and transport of powders becomes more frequent and the number of fires or explosions reported is increasing. In a systematic hazard analysis the charge on the bulked product as well as the charge on the FIBC must be considered. As far as the explosion atmosphere is concerned again both the atmosphere in the FIBC and the atmosphere in the surroundings must be analysed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer aided solution of electrostatic field problems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrostatic Problems During Material Handling
abstract: Summary form only given. The status of the finite element method is demonstrated by examples of results from commercial software. New developments and advances are highlighted, with a short survey of CAD systems and an assessment of the role of computer modelling in electrostatics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrostatic ignition risk in powder processing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electrostatic Problems During Material Handling
abstract: Electrostatic charge levels generated on organic powders in typical operations are tabulated and typical ignition energy values in millijoules are listed, with safety measures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
